quarterly_data.quarter: Analog Devices U.S. All Stars Conference 2026 (09-22-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: CFO Rich Puccio on the outlook: based on demand signals, bookings and backlog, ADI sees 'an opportunity for sustained growth in the double digits, even into 2027' and expects double-digit growth again in the upcoming year, while cautioning that the macro environment is uncertain. He does not guide Q1, but with what ADI sees today he expects it 'can deliver an above-seasonal Q1' - Q1 is normally down in the mid-single digits. Bookings are now arriving further out into the second quarter, giving more visibility than six months ago, which matters because wafer starts are made six months ahead of delivery. Design wins in 2026 are on track to exceed the growth rates of 2025, with outsized growth in data center and aerospace and defense.
quarterly_data.figure: double-digit growth into 2027; above-seasonal Q1 (normally down mid-single digits)

quarterly_data.quarter: Analog Devices U.S. All Stars Conference 2026 (09-22-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: CFO Rich Puccio on the 'super cycle' businesses (ATE, aerospace and defense, data center - essentially 30% of ADI): the aerospace and defense exit rate at Q3 is nearing $2 billion annualized (a year ago the business was just getting to $1 billion), spanning LEO and geosynchronous satellites, drones and missile defense, and he believes it can grow double digits for the next decade. ATE exited Q3 at an annualized run rate of just about $1 billion; each generation of more complex testers for HBM and high-performance compute drives more ADI content. He confirmed data center as 'a $2 billion run rate business' in power and optical. In these three areas ADI is already shipping above the historical consumption line, but he does not believe customers are building inventory there; more than 50% of industrial sub-segments are still double digits below consumption.
quarterly_data.figure: A&D exit rate nearing $2 billion (vs $1 billion a year ago); ATE ~$1 billion run rate; data center $2 billion run rate

quarterly_data.quarter: Analog Devices U.S. All Stars Conference 2026 (09-22-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: CFO Rich Puccio on pricing, inventory and capacity: ADI has taken two price increases this year, both framed as cost recovery with no margin stacking - the first largely targeted at the channel, the second rolled out in mid-September broadly across all customers, driven by inflation that has broadened into wafer costs and assembly pricing; no incremental pricing actions are planned, though ADI would consider one if inflation materially affects it. ADI ended Q3 with record gross inventory and expects to add more in Q4 with days likely flat; channel inventory is expected to end slightly below six weeks despite additions because sell-through is accelerating. Factories are running 'pretty hot': ADI is adding capacity every day (equipment into available clean rooms, test capability and more external capacity), so utilization is not expected to be a further margin driver. The 34% to 40% free cash flow margin model stands, with the aim of reaching its high end.
quarterly_data.figure: second price increase mid-September across all customers; channel slightly below six weeks; FCF model 34% to 40%

quarterly_data.quarter: Analog Devices U.S. All Stars Conference 2026 (09-22-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: CFO Rich Puccio on the Alif Semiconductor acquisition (announced two weeks earlier, not yet closed): Alif brings an AI-native heterogeneous compute platform that accelerates ADI's physical-intelligence / edge-AI strategy and pulls more of the ADI portfolio into integrated solutions; ADI does not expect it to be near-term material to revenue or cost, and sees the business ramping more in the 2028 timeframe.
quarterly_data.figure: not near-term material; ramps more in the 2028 timeframe

players.product: optical CONTROL path - timing, power management, data conversion, monitoring & control for lasers/transceivers, OCS and CPO

quarterly_data.quarter: Analog Devices U.S. All Stars Conference 2026 (09-22-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: CFO Rich Puccio: ADI's primary optical position is the optical control system that controls the lasers, where it has held a leading position and tended to set the standard; it has had very strong positions at 400 and 800 and is 'already shipping a 1.6 terabit solution into the market', with customers already working on the next speed. Each speed generation gives ADI a chance to gain share and content. Data center optical and power are growing at similar rates today, but he expects power growth to exceed optical over time as ADI builds a vertical-power position, moving the mix away from 50/50.

players.product: grid-to-chip power - grid monitoring & BMS, 800V-to-intermediate conversion, intermediate-to-core rails and Empower IVR vertical power delivery

quarterly_data.quarter: Analog Devices U.S. All Stars Conference 2026 (09-22-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: CFO Rich Puccio: inside the data center ADI plays in power management (hot swap), power conversion (stepping high voltages down to intermediate) and the 'last micron' of stage 2 power delivery into the chip, where the Empower acquisition gives it an IVR vertical power product that avoids the losses of lateral delivery. ADI's analysis says it can save 15%+ power loss, and he called stage 2 power delivery probably ADI's biggest long-term growth opportunity in the data center.
